findings.source_passage: Look at that hanging lower lip! what a huge sulk and pout is there! a sulk and pout, by carpenter's measurement, about twenty feet long
findings.why_it_matters: The triple repetition of 'sulk and pout' is a distinctively rhetorical, voice-establishing riff; the draft preserves the first two instances but the triple anaphoric pattern is intact—this is borderline acceptable, but the surrounding buildup ('a very sulky looking fellow to grace a diadem') is flattened to 'though a sulky one,' erasing the mock-regal irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'a very sulky looking fellow to grace a diadem' before the lip description to preserve the ironic register.

findings.source_passage: One voyager in Purchas calls them the wondrous 'whiskers' inside of the whale's mouth; another, 'hogs' bristles'; a third old gentleman in Hackluyt uses the following elegant language
findings.why_it_matters: The mock-scholarly citation of Purchas and Hackluyt by name, with the ironic 'following elegant language,' is part of Ishmael's characteristic antiquarian voice; the draft collapses it to 'Old travelers called them whiskers, hogs' bristles, fins,' losing both the named sources and the ironic framing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the named sources (Purchas, Hackluyt) and the phrase 'following elegant language' to preserve the antiquarian irony.

findings.source_passage: This reminds us that the Right Whale really has a sort of whisker, or rather a moustache, consisting of a few scattered white hairs… impart a rather brigandish expression to his otherwise solemn countenance.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'brigandish expression' footnote is a signature Ishmaelean comic aside with distinctive character-description rhetoric; its complete absence removes a characteristic voice moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert a brief version of the moustache/brigandish-expression aside, even compressed, to maintain Ishmael's comic-digressive voice.

findings.source_passage: the demand has long been on the decline… And as those ancient dames moved about gaily, though in the jaws of the whale
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the key ironic sentences about dames and umbrellas nearly verbatim, which is good, but omits the setup about demand being 'on the decline,' slightly weakening the comic structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor: add 'the demand has long been on the decline' before the Queen Anne sentence to restore the ironic contrast.

findings.source_passage: Can you catch the expression of the Sperm Whale's there? It is the same he died with, only some of the longer wrinkles in the forehead seem now faded away.
findings.why_it_matters: The elegiac opening of the final meditation—'It is the same he died with'—is an interpretively significant detail lending pathos to the philosophical comparison; its omission makes the Stoic/Platonian conclusion feel abrupt.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'the same expression he died with, only some longer wrinkles faded away' before the prairie-placidity phrase.

summary: The draft preserves the major signature passages (sulk-and-pout anaphora, Jonah/wigwam, Haarlem organ, Stoic/Platonian) but flattens the antiquarian citation voice (Purchas/Hackluyt), omits the 'brigandish expression' aside entirely, and strips some ironic framing; findings are medium/low severity, not reaching the regeneration threshold.
